messages:
sam: FYI shelf-17 / slice-dedicated-45 showing sustained NVMe io stall + host cpu steal starting 03:14 UTC. 99p gen latency up, some customer timeouts. Posting here for triage.
maria: saw the io_slowdown alerts. kvcache write amplification spikes correlate with a few tenants doing parallel large uploads. suspect mlprep + dataset ingestion.
aj: can we rate-limit writers at the proxy to soften the NVMe tail? suggestion: egress shaping + short-lived write-cgroup on hosts for heavy io tenants. Example quick command to throttle tenant egress at router: 
```
# limit tenant 824 to 80Mbps via router API
curl -X POST http://router-api.local/v1/tenants/824/egress \
  -d '{"bandwidth_mbps":80}'
```
noah: +1 to router-side shaping. Also propose temporary host-side io_cgroup policy to cap write_iops for offending container to 2000 iops. That avoids moving tenants immediately and reduces migration churn.
rachel: if shaping doesn't bring 99p below 300ms in 10m, plan B is ephemeral carveout: create an ephemeral fractional slice and move offending tenant there for 30-60m to replay and confirm. Migration play: pause new allocs -> live-migrate KV shard -> resume. Ops-runbook link: https://internal.redwood/ops/runbooks/io-noise.
maria: can infra-bot run a quick query to identify top 5 write-heavy tenants on shelf-17 in last 15m? I have a suspicion around tenant-824 and tenant-1503.
infra-bot: query result: top_write_tenants: ["tenant-824","tenant-1503","tenant-993","tenant-402"] (from 03:00-03:15 UTC). avg_write_iops: [5400, 4200, 2100, 800].
aj: thanks. i'll kick a 5% router fallback to warm-reserve to shed immediate tail while we apply shaping to the top 2 tenants. command: 
```
# apply 5% fallback from slice-dedicated-45
curl -X POST http://router-api.local/v1/routing/fallback -d '{"from":"slice-dedicated-45","to":"warm-reserve-eu1","fraction":0.05}'
```
noah: when you apply fallback, also tag telemetry with tag=io-fallback-1723459990 so dashboards show effect.
rachel: cost note: warm-reserve delta is ~+$600/hr while fallback active. ops accept? we have 3h buffer in incident budget.
sam: approve up to 2h fallback. keep finance informed if >2h. Also add SLI alert: shelf_io_depth > 75% for 3m -> paged to eng-infra.
maria: implemented router shaping for tenant-824 & tenant-1503 (80Mbps / 120Mbps). watching metrics.
infra-bot: 03:18 UTC fallback applied (5%). 99p latency down from ~2.1s -> ~380ms within 75s. nvme_write_q depth trending down. alert-id: alert-1723459990.
aj: canary looks good. after 10m, if stable, increase fallback to 25% and keep shaping. Also recommend an automatic quarantine rule: if a tenant causes >3 sustained nvme spikes (30m windows) in 24h, auto-quarantine to a fractional slice and notify account team.
noah: logging note: please capture host iostat + dmesg + router logs to INF-8492. I'll run the isolation migration at 03:50 UTC if we still see noise.
sam: great. INF-8492 created; marking severity: high. everyone paste short notes there. If warm-reserve shows >700ms revert fallback to 0% immediately.
(many reactions: :thumbsup:, :eyes: )
